description: Single-panel line chart of phase volume fraction versus annealing temperature for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel (no panel letters; the group is one plot). The y-axis is labelled "Phase Volume Fraction" with ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0; the x-axis is labelled "Temperature (°C)" with labelled ticks HR, 700, 800, 900, 1000, 1100 and 1200, and axis-break marks ("//") on both the bottom and top spines between HR and 700. A legend at the top right maps red squares to α, blue triangles to γ and orange stars to κ; matching coloured Greek labels (γ in blue, α in red, κ in orange) are also printed inside the plot area. The red α curve starts near the 0.5 gridline at HR, peaks at 700 °C above the 0.8 gridline, falls through roughly 0.52 at 850 °C to about 0.4 at 900–950 °C, then stays nearly flat between the 0.2 and 0.4 gridlines up to 1200 °C. The blue γ curve is about 0.48 at HR, drops to exactly 0.0 at 700 °C, rises steeply to about 0.6 at 900 °C, plateaus near 0.6–0.63 up to ~1050 °C and declines slightly to ~0.57 at 1200 °C. The orange κ curve exists only between 700 and ~850 °C, decreasing from ~0.15 to ~0.02, with a dashed extrapolation to zero at 900 °C. The figure therefore demonstrates that α and κ-carbide dissolve while γ grows between 700 and 900 °C, κ-carbide becoming undetectable at 900 °C. No individual data values are printed on any point.

subfigures.description: Line-and-symbol plot of Phase Volume Fraction (y, 0.0–1.0) against Temperature (x, HR to 1200 °C, axis broken between HR and 700 °C) with three series: α (red squares), γ (blue triangles) and κ (orange stars). α peaks above the 0.8 gridline at 700 °C then falls to ~0.4 at 900 °C and stays flat; γ falls to 0.0 at 700 °C, rises to ~0.6 at 900 °C and plateaus to ~0.57 at 1200 °C; κ decreases from ~0.15 at 700 °C and reaches zero at 900 °C (dashed segment).

observations.observation: The plot's y-axis is labelled "Phase Volume Fraction" and runs 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.2; the x-axis is labelled "Temperature (°C)" with ticks HR, 700, 800, 900, 1000, 1100 and 1200.
The x-axis is broken between HR and 700 °C, marked by a double-slash symbol on both the bottom and top spines, so the HR datum is not on the same linear temperature scale as the annealed specimens.

The legend defines red squares = α, blue triangles = γ and orange stars = κ, and the same Greek letters are printed in the matching colours inside the plot area (γ near 900–1000 °C, α near 1000–1050 °C, κ near 800 °C).

The α (red square) curve rises from about the 0.5 level at HR to its maximum at 700 °C, which lies above the 0.8 gridline, then decreases to roughly the 0.4 gridline at 900 °C and remains nearly flat between the 0.2 and 0.4 gridlines up to 1200 °C.

The γ (blue triangle) curve sits near 0.48 at HR, falls to exactly 0.0 at 700 °C (symbol plotted on the x-axis), then rises steeply through ~0.3 and ~0.4 to about the 0.6 gridline at 900 °C, plateaus around 0.6–0.63 up to ~1050 °C and declines slightly to ~0.57 at 1200 °C.
The κ (orange star) curve is plotted only for the 700–850 °C interval, descending from ~0.15 to ~0.02, and is continued by a dashed segment that reaches 0.0 at 900 °C.
No numeric value is printed next to any data point; fractions can only be read against the y-axis gridlines.
The caption states that the κ-carbide cannot be detected by XRD in the specimen annealed at 900 °C, which is consistent with the κ curve reaching zero at 900 °C.
The citing text states that the volume-fraction change of each phase is determined from the XRD measurement results and that the general trend is similar to that calculated by Thermo-Calc (Fig. 1).
The citing text states that no γ phase is detected when the annealing temperature is 700 °C, matching the γ datum plotted at 0.0 at 700 °C.

The citing text reports that at 900 °C the γ phase fraction is about 60%, and that the γ fraction varies only in the small range 57% to 63% between 900 °C and 1200 °C, reaching its largest value around 1000 °C.
The citing text states that when the annealing temperature changes from 700 °C to 900 °C the volume fractions of α phase and κ-carbide decrease and the fraction of γ phase increases.

The citing text states that the κ-carbide dissolution temperature lies between 850 °C and 900 °C, higher than the 823 °C calculated by Thermo-Calc, and that the boundary κ-carbide seen in Fig. 10 could not be detected by XRD probably because its fraction is too small.
The citing text states that the phase fractions of α and γ change only a little in a narrow range above 900 °C, which is why they are not considered the main cause of the tensile-property change.

unreadable_items: Intermediate data-point temperatures (e.g. 750, 850, 950, 1050, 1150 °C) are not printed on the x-axis; their positions are inferred only from the spacing between labelled ticks.
No numeric values are printed for any data point, so all fractions are read against the y-axis gridlines only.
The HR tick lies beyond the axis break and its exact temperature is not given in the figure.
